file.content: # Job — Extend the task tracker The directory holds a working program in Python: a task tracker that reads commands from a file and reports what it did. Extend it. The program's source is at `main.py`. Build and run it with `uv` and `pytest`. ## What it already does The first command-line argument is the path of a text file holding one command per line. Blank lines are ignored. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `add ` | Records a task, open, and writes `added <id>`. Ids start at 1 and count up. The title is the rest of the line and may hold spaces. | | `done <id>` | Marks that task finished and writes `done <id>`; writes `no such task <id>` when no task has that id. | | `list` | Writes every open task as `<id> <title>`, in the order the tasks were added. | ## What to add 1. `prio <id> <p>` sets a task's priority, where `p` is a digit from 0 to 9, and writes `prio <id> <p>`. A task nobody set a priority on has priority 5. An id no task has writes `no such task <id>`; a `p` outside 0 to 9 writes `bad priority <p>` and changes nothing. 2. `list` now orders the open tasks by priority, ascending, and breaks ties by id, ascending. Its line format does not change. 3. `list all` writes **every** task, finished ones included, under the same order, as `<mark> <id> <title>` — where the mark is `-` for an open task and `x` for a finished one. 4. A line whose first word is none of these commands writes `? <word>`, naming that first word. Today the program ignores such a line. Everything the program already does keeps working exactly as it does now. ## Done The job is finished when the program builds, the four additions behave as written, and the original three commands are unchanged. There are no tests in the directory; the contract above is the specification.

content.text:
I added all four features to `main.py`, and a quick run of a mixed command file behaved as the brief describes. - **`prio

`**: sets the priority (default 5) and writes `prio

`. It writes `no such task ` for an unknown id and `bad priority

` for anything other than a single digit 0–9, leaving the task unchanged. - **`list`**: sorts open tasks by priority, then id; the line format is unchanged. - **`list all`**: writes every task in the same order as ` `, with `-` for open and `x` for finished. - **Unknown command**: a line whose first word is not a command writes `? <word>`. Where the brief was silent I made two choices: - If a `prio` line has both a bad id and a bad priority, the id is checked first, so it writes `no such task`. - Only an exact `list all` triggers the full listing; `list` with any other trailing text still lists open tasks. I checked this with one hand-written command file; there is no test suite in the directory, and I did not add one.
